title: Copy types
summary: Small scalar types duplicate on assignment instead of moving - no ownership transfer.
lecture: Types that implement Copy - i32, u64, f64, bool, char, shared references, small tuples of Copy types - are duplicated bit-for-bit when assigned or passed. The original stays fully usable; there is no move, ever.

That is why passing an i32 to a function and using it afterwards just works, while doing the same with a String is E0382. Heap-owning types (String, Vec, Box) can't be Copy: duplicating them bit-for-bit would create two owners of one allocation.
Corollary: calling .clone() on a Copy value is pointless - it costs nothing but says nothing. If the compiler never complains about reusing a value, stop cloning it.

example.caption: Same syntax, opposite semantics - the type decides.
